routing.reason: A small feature with testable acceptance criteria: one nullable column, one validation, a date shown and a date field on the one-page UI, with tests and README, and no security stake.
rulings: Ruling: workflow `direct` — S ticket with six testable acceptance criteria, about 5 small files (src/db.ts, src/tasks.ts, src/app.ts, public/*, test, README), no authentication, permissions, payments, personal data or secrets, so one developer can do it in one go — cost if wrong: a missed cross-cutting issue comes up only at the short review, and the run would need to be re-routed to `default`.

Ruling: product owner, PM, architect, UX, SEO and security review left out — acceptance criteria are already testable, the design is a plain date input next to existing controls, there are no public SEO pages, and a date string validated server-side and bound as a SQL parameter carries no security stake — cost if wrong: a small accessibility or layout gap on the add form, or a validation edge case, caught only at the visual or code review.

Ruling: one task for the `back` role (covers AC1–AC6), since most of the work is in the API, the migration and the tests; the small UI change in public/app.js and public/index.html goes with it — cost if wrong: the UI part gets less front-end care; the visual review step would catch it.

Ruling: the migration is a new entry appended to `migrations` in src/db.ts (`ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT`), never an edit of the shipped first one — the file says so, and AC4 requires existing databases to keep working; the dba migration review runs as in the workflow — cost if wrong: existing databases would not migrate.

Ruling: PATCH must tell an absent `due_date` (leave as is) from `null` (clear it); the current `changes.x ?? task.x` pattern in updateTask cannot, so the developer must test for the key's presence (`'due_date' in body`) — cost if wrong: a PATCH of `done` alone would wipe the date, or null would never clear it.

Ruling: validation accepts only a string of exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` that round-trips as a real calendar date (leap years included, `2026-02-30` rejected); any other type (number, object) also gets the 400 with the exact message, checked before anything is saved, on both POST and PATCH — cost if wrong: invalid dates stored or a wrong status code.

Ruling: budget $0.70 — one S task, a short review, the dba migration review and the visual check, with some margin for one fix round — cost if wrong: the run stops before the reviews and the user must approve more.

task.goal: Add an optional `due_date` to tasks. (1) src/db.ts: append a NEW migration to the `migrations` array (never edit the shipped first one), e.g. `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT`, so existing rows get NULL. (2) src/tasks.ts: add `due_date: string | null` to `Task` and `Row`; `createTask(db, title, due_date?)` stores it; `updateTask` must distinguish an absent `due_date` (keep the current value) from `null` (clear it): do not use `??` for this field, test for the key's presence. (3) src/app.ts: POST passes `body.due_date`, PATCH passes it only when the key is present in the body; validate in one place: `due_date` must be a string matching `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` and a real calendar date (for example build a Date from the parts and compare year, month and day; `2026-02-30` is invalid, leap days are valid), `null` is allowed (and means no date on POST); anything else (`2026-1-5`, `tomorrow`, a number, an object) answers 400 with exactly `{"error": "due_date must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format"}` and saves nothing (validate before any write, on POST and PATCH, and a PATCH with an invalid date must not change the title or done either). Keep the existing 404 behaviour for an unknown id. (4) public/index.html and public/app.js: add an optional `<input type="date">` with a label to the add form (send `due_date` as null when empty, and reset it with the form), and show the due date next to the title in `taskItem` only when the task has one (text content only, no innerHTML). (5) test/tasks.test.ts, in the existing style: default null, create with a date, create without, PATCH sets, PATCH clears with null, PATCH without due_date leaves it, invalid formats and a non-existent day get 400 with the exact message and nothing saved (POST creates no task; PATCH leaves the task unchanged), and a database at the old schema version 1 (a task already in it) migrates and returns `due_date: null`. (6) README.md: document the `due_date` field, its format, null, the POST and PATCH behaviour and the 400 error. Run `npm test` and make it pass.

criteria.why: Migration adds due_date TEXT, Task interface and toTask spread expose it, null by default.
POST passes due_date; PATCH uses 'in' check to set, clear with null, or keep when absent.
validDueDate checks regex and real calendar day, returns 400 with exact message before any write; tests cover it for POST and PATCH.
New migration appended; test migrates a version-1 DB and checks null due_date.
app.js renders a <time> element next to the title and the form has a date input sent on submit.
Tests added for default, create, patch, invalid values, migration; README documents the field and error.

findings.what: PATCH uses `"due_date" in body`; if the body is JSON null or a non-object (e.g. `null`, a number), `in` throws a TypeError or readJson yields null and it surfaces as a 500. Pre-existing readJson weakness, but the new code adds another crash point.
Invalid JSON bodies and non-object bodies are still not turned into a 400; not part of this ticket but the new validation does not cover them.
Frontend changes (date input, time element, sending null when empty) have no test; the page test only checks the h1.
`...(due ? [due] : [])` spread is a convoluted way to optionally append an element.
Validation lives in app.ts while tasks.ts accepts any string, so the data layer is unprotected if called from elsewhere.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion with careful date validation (including leap years and years 0–99), a proper migration, and thorough tests covering POST, PATCH, invalid inputs, and migration of an existing database. Remaining issues are minor: non-object JSON bodies can still crash the PATCH path, the UI has no test, and a small readability wart in app.js.
